text: The Uttar Pradesh Janhit Guarantee Act, 2011 notifies time-bound delivery of specified public services (such as drinking water handpump repairs, basic sanitation, and street lighting) typically within 7 to 30 days depending on the service schedule.

Under the UP Panchayati Raj Act, 1947, the Block Development Officer (BDO) and District Panchayat Raj Officer (DPRO) exercise administrative and supervisory functions over Gram Panchayat civic operations and panchayat secretaries.

If a civic grievance is not addressed by the local block or municipal office within the notified timeframe, citizens may present an appeal to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM), Chief Development Officer (CDO), or District Magistrate (DM) during Tehsil Samadhan Diwas.

Sampoorna Samadhan Diwas (Tehsil Diwas) is organized in Uttar Pradesh tehsils on designated Saturdays (typically the 1st and 3rd Saturdays of the month, or subject to local district administration scheduling).
On the UP IGRS Jansunwai portal (jansunwai.up.nic.in), citizens can track registered grievances and submit official reminders if a complaint is unresolved after the statutory resolution period.

Under the Right to Information Act, 2005 and UP RTI Rules, an RTI application for public records can be submitted to the Public Information Officer (PIO) with a statutory application fee of Rs 10 (payable online on rtionline.up.gov.in, or by court fee stamp / IPO / treasury challan offline).
The Government of Uttar Pradesh operates the toll-free CM Helpline 1076 for telephone registration and status inquiries of citizen grievances across the state.
